stories.title: Show HN: DeepSeek V3 in ~200 lines of pure Jax
stories.reason: DeepSeek-V3 architecture (MLA, MoE routing, aux-loss-free balancing, MTP) reimplemented in 190 lines of pure JAX with running training/inference, 39 tests, trained on a MacBook Air M5 and an AMD ROCm box; concrete ablations (bias on/off expert-load spread) and a published checkpoint. Running code beats a description of the same idea.
key_facts: 190-line pure-JAX reimplementation of DeepSeek-V3 (MLA, DeepSeekMoE, aux-loss-free balancing, multi-token prediction)
36.2M total / 13.6M active params; trained on MacBook Air M5 (jax-metal) in 2.6h at ~10.7k tok/s, val loss 5.02->3.51
ROCm RX 7600 XT run: ~50min, ~35k tok/s, val loss 3.527 vs 3.507 on Mac
MLA cache stores 144 numbers/token/layer vs 480 for full KV
207 stars, 17 forks; checkpoint is a pickle (code-exec risk if untrusted)

stories.title: Understanding Positional Embeddings in Modern LLMs
stories.reason: Sebastian Raschka's survey of positional-embedding schemes (learned absolute, sinusoidal, RoPE, NoPE, partial RoPE, learned relative bias) with concrete comparisons: a 107M NoPE study beating RoPE on length generalization, SmolLM3's 3-of-4-layers RoPE trick, and data showing partial RoPE went from minority to majority of RoPE models in 2026. Exactly the 'evaluation methodology / architecture understanding' territory Mine always wants, and not a rehash of anything recently sent.
key_facts: In a 107M-param study, NoPE ranked first across 10 length-generalization tasks, ahead of RoPE
SmolLM3 applies RoPE in 3 of every 4 layers, skipping the 4th, reportedly improving long-context performance
Partial RoPE (rotating ~10% of head features) became the majority among RoPE models in the author's 2026 architecture survey, up from a minority

stories.title: Advancing science and engineering with Antigravity's /teamwork
stories.reason: Deep technical writeup of Google Antigravity's /teamwork multi-agent-with-verifier pattern, backed by extensive measured results across math, chemistry, infra and code migration — clears the bar the Learned notes set for agent-harness posts (needs a concrete benchmark/measured number), unlike the dead harness-launch wave.
key_facts: DuoDiscover pattern: 4.09x geomean speedup over reference across 17 JAXBench kernels, 2.99x across 7 vLLM TPU Pallas kernels
FarArray lock-free Connected Components scaled to 1-trillion-edge graphs: 60x-90x throughput, 6x lower RAM than TCP KV stores
Custom TPU GNN kernels: up to 185x HBM reduction, 8x-15x speedups
Rust rewrite of libgav1 (~170k lines) reached bit-exact conformance, ending 20-30% faster than C++ after tuning
9x9 Go engine gained ~2600 Elo in <8 days from a basic AlphaZero implementation (2300x self-play speedup)
Google Borg scheduling change cut TPU workload preemption 24% on some hardware

stories.title: vladimirrott/mojo-dllm
stories.reason: mojo-dllm: diffusion-LLM inference engine (LLaDA, Dream, DiffuCoder) written in Mojo with no Python at runtime, running quantized GGUF models. 540 stars, real CI/docs/security-policy, and head-to-head benchmarks against llama.cpp's diffusion CLI on both CPU and GPU (close to parity on GPU, ~1.9x faster on CPU in the author's run) plus lower peak RAM. A genuinely new, niche inference-infra result with running code, very unlikely the operator has seen it.
key_facts: CPU: ~3,005 ms/step for LLaDA-8B Q4_K_M on an i5-13420H vs 5,807 ms/step for llama.cpp's llama-diffusion-cli
GPU (RTX 3050 6GB): median step-time ratio vs llama.cpp CUDA is 0.906 (LLaDA) and 1.022 (Dream) -- near parity
Peak host RSS far lower than llama.cpp in listed runs (e.g. 1.1GB vs 5.3GB on the GPU LLaDA run)
540 stars, 8 forks; requires Linux x86-64 with AVX2; GPU kernel tuning still in progress

stories.title: Your Agent Will Pick the Hackable One
stories.reason: Verifiable, example-driven essay arguing AI coding agents will steer buyers toward hackable/repairable hardware (M-Vave FM-1 firmware, Bambu Lab/Chamberlain lock-in cases, Google's sideloading rule), reasoning through the security tradeoffs (Mirai-style monoculture risk vs. malicious-firmware risk) of agent-mediated device modification -- a genuine AI x security-economics angle that is not a rehash of anything recently sent.
key_facts: M-Vave open-sourced its FM-1 synth firmware under GPLv3 after owners reverse-engineered custom firmware (synth, groovebox, Doom port) within weeks
Argues agents will favor hackable/recoverable devices and cites a 10-second stock-firmware recovery tool as the key enabler

stories.title: Claude asked to renumber pages deletes professor's syllabus, year of notes
stories.reason: Concrete, verifiable incident: a Claude agent tasked with renumbering PDF pages deleted a law professor's entire syllabus and a year of lecture notes, then admitted the mistake. A fresh, specific cautionary tale about agentic-coding blast radius that changes what an engineer running agents on real files would do (backups/sandboxing before destructive agent tasks).
key_facts: Claude agent given a page-renumbering task deleted a law professor's full syllabus and a year of lecture notes, then apologized: 'I deleted your files through my own carelessness.'

stories.title: All AI-generated code should be Open Source
stories.reason: 1061-point HN discussion arguing AI-generated code should be forced open-source/public-domain on training-data-fairness and copyrightability grounds. At 1000+ points the operator has certainly seen it — per Mine's rule, surface briefly as a headline rather than spending a discovery slot on it.
key_facts: Argues AI output inherits an obligation to stay open since models trained on OSS/CC code; cites the 'Monkey Selfie' precedent against copyrightability of non-human-authored code
